text.en: Ainu lacks the grammatical category of tense, and past, present, and future tenses are not morphologically marked on the verb ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--absence-of-tense-category⟧⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--no-morphological-tense-marking-on-verbs⟧. The verbal system contains no affix marking tense, making no distinction comparable to present versus past in English ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-ainu-verbal-system-does-not-possess-any⟧. In Southwestern Hokkaido Ainu, verbs possess no pure tense markers ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--verbs-lack-pure-tense-markers⟧. Because the language does not locate utterances on a linear time concept, forms like *oman* signify only the verbal concept in connection with person without inherently expressing past or present tense ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-lacks-the-grammatical-category-of-tense-and⟧. Simple verb forms refer to events irrespective of their time in relation to the time of utterance ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-simple-verb-form-in-ainu-refers-to⟧. Consequently, verbs such as *apkas* can be translated with either present or past tense meaning depending on the actual situation and context ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-verbs-such-as-apkas-can-be-translated⟧. Since verbs do not inflect for tense, whether a relative clause refers to present or future or past action is determined by context ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-verbs-do-not-inflect-for-tense-so⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, marking past, present, and future is not obligatory, and tense often cannot be determined from the verb form alone ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-marking-of-past-present-and-future-is⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, no form actively indicates tense, and the bare verb form can express that the action is certain, whether in the present or in the past ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-ainu-there-is-no-form-that-actively⟧. In that variety, the zero auxiliary verb *φ* expresses past tense or habitual action, signifying 'did, always does' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-zero-auxiliary-verb-expresses-past-tense-or⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には時制という文法範疇が存在せず、動詞には過去・現在・未来の時制が形態的に表示されない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--absence-of-tense-category⟧⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--no-morphological-tense-marking-on-verbs⟧。動詞体系には時制を表示する接辞は一切存在せず、英語における現在と過去のような区別も持たない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-ainu-verbal-system-does-not-possess-any⟧。北海道南西部アイヌ語において、動詞には純粋な時制標識が存在しない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--verbs-lack-pure-tense-markers⟧。アイヌ語は線形的な時間概念に関与しないため、*oman*のような形は本質的に過去時制や現在時制を表すものではなく、単に人称に関連した動詞概念を表すにすぎない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-lacks-the-grammatical-category-of-tense-and⟧。単純動詞形は、発話時との時間的関係に関わりなく事象を指示する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-simple-verb-form-in-ainu-refers-to⟧。したがって、*apkas*のような動詞は状況や前後の文脈に応じて現在の意味にも過去の意味にも訳すことができる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-verbs-such-as-apkas-can-be-translated⟧。動詞は時制による変化を行わないため、連体修飾節が現在・未来か過去の行為を指すかは文脈によって判断される⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--ainu-verbs-do-not-inflect-for-tense-so⟧。北海道アイヌ語では過去、現在、未来の表示は義務的ではなく、動詞の形を見ただけでは時間的判断がつかない場合が少なくない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-marking-of-past-present-and-future-is⟧。樺太アイヌ語では積極的に時制を表示する形式はなく、動詞の裸の形は表される行為が確定的なことを現在でも過去でも表すことができる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-ainu-there-is-no-form-that-actively⟧。同方言では、ゼロ助動詞*φ*が過去時制や習慣的な行為（「～た、いつも～する」）を表す⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-zero-auxiliary-verb-expresses-past-tense-or⟧。

text.en: Kindaichi asserts that the Ainu language makes no temporal distinctions and expresses everything in the past tense ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--kindaichi-asserts-that-the-ainu-language-makes-no⟧. By contrast, Chiri argues for Sakhalin Ainu that only non-stative verbs require translation as past tense when isolated in direct mood, whereas stative verbs should be translated as present progressive ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--chiri-argues-for-sakhalin-ainu-that-only-non⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects of Southwestern Hokkaido, the auxiliary verbs *a* and *aan* basically express past tense in terms of tense ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-terms-of-tense-the-auxiliary-verbs-a⟧.
text.ja: 金田一は、アイヌ語は時間的区別を行わず、すべてを過去形で表現すると主張する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--kindaichi-asserts-that-the-ainu-language-makes-no⟧。これに対して知里は、樺太アイヌ語において直接法で単独で述語となる場合、非持続態動詞のみが過去形と訳されるべきであり、持続態動詞は現在進行形（「〜ている」）と訳されるべきであると論じる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--chiri-argues-for-sakhalin-ainu-that-only-non⟧。北海道南西部の沙流方言および千歳方言においては、テンスの観点から助動詞*a*および*aan*が基本的に過去を表す⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-terms-of-tense-the-auxiliary-verbs-a⟧。

text.en: In Ainu, temporal relations relative to the speech time can be indicated through time adverbs, expressions of volition or necessity for the future, sentence-final phrases for the present, and forms expressing completion for the past ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-ainu-temporal-relations-relative-to-the-speech⟧. Points in time can be directly expressed using adverbs that indicate temporal relations, such as *numan* 'yesterday' or *nisatta* 'tomorrow' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--points-in-time-can-be-directly-expressed-using⟧. Without such adverbs as *numan* 'yesterday' or *nisatta* 'tomorrow', the same clause can be understood as either future or past depending on context ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--without-a-time-adverb-like-numan-yesterday-or⟧. In Southwestern Hokkaido Ainu, lexical expressions of temporal deixis such as *tane* and *tan-ukuran* do not undergo a deictic shift in semi-direct reported discourse ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-semi-direct-reported-discourse-lexical-expressions-of⟧. In the Shizunai dialect of Southwestern Hokkaido, the morpheme *nisa* is not found ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-morpheme-nisa-is-not-found-in-the⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, a bare verb can be used together with a past time adverb to state a fact that occurred in the past, and bare verbs can also express habitual actions ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--to-state-a-fact-that-occurred-in-the⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the adverb *tane* centers on 'right now' but encompasses a relatively wide span of 'now', including a little before and a little after the present ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-tane-centers-on-right-now-but⟧. The Hokkaido adverb *tap* appears to be used only for immediate past events occurring a little before the present ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-tap-appears-to-be-used-only⟧. It appears in the fixed expressions *tap oro wano* and *tap oro wa un* with the meaning 'after that', referring to a time after a reference point in the past ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-form-tap-is-used-in-the-fixed⟧. Furthermore, *tap* combines with other adverbs in forms such as *tap tane*, *tap tanto*, and *tap núman* to express meanings like 'just now', 'having just ... today', or 'just yesterday' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-form-tap-can-combine-with-other-adverbs⟧. Among other Hokkaido temporal expressions, the adverb *ésir* means 'a little while ago' or 'just before' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-sir-means-a-little-while-ago⟧. The adverb *teta* means 'the other day' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-teta-means-the-other-day⟧. The temporal noun and adverb *teeta* means 'long ago' or 'in the past' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-noun-adverb-teeta-means-long-ago⟧. In addition, the temporal adverb *tanto* means 'today' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-tanto-means-today⟧, *núman* means 'yesterday' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-n-man-means-yesterday⟧, and *nisatta* means 'tomorrow' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-nisatta-means-tomorrow⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語において発話時点との時間関係を示す手段には、時間副詞を用いること、未来を表すために意志や必然性を表す形式を用いること、現在を表すために文末句を用いること、過去を表すために完了を表す形式を用いることがある⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-ainu-temporal-relations-relative-to-the-speech⟧。時点は*numan*「昨日」や*nisatta*「明日」といった時間関係を表す副詞を用いて直接表すことができる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--points-in-time-can-be-directly-expressed-using⟧。*numan*「昨日」や*nisatta*「明日」のような時間副詞を伴わない場合、同一の節が文脈次第で未来の話にも過去の話にも理解され得る⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--without-a-time-adverb-like-numan-yesterday-or⟧。北海道南西部アイヌ語の半直接話法において、*tane*や*tan-ukuran*などの時間直示を表す語彙表現は直示シフトを起こさない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--in-semi-direct-reported-discourse-lexical-expressions-of⟧。北海道南西部の静内方言には形態素*nisa*が見られない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-morpheme-nisa-is-not-found-in-the⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、過去に起こった事実を述べる際に過去を表す時の副詞などを添えて動詞をそのまま用いることができ、習慣的な行為にも動詞がそのまま用いられる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--to-state-a-fact-that-occurred-in-the⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、副詞*tane*は「今現在」を軸としつつも、少し前や少し後を含めた比較的幅広い「今」を意味する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-tane-centers-on-right-now-but⟧。副詞*tap*は「今より少し前」の直近の過去の出来事に限って用いられるようである⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-tap-appears-to-be-used-only⟧。この*tap*は固定表現*tap oro wano*や*tap oro wa un*において過去の基準点以後の「それから」という意味で用いられる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-form-tap-is-used-in-the-fixed⟧。また、*tap*は他の副詞と組み合わされて*tap tane*、*tap tanto*、*tap núman*のように「つい今しがた」、「今日〜したばかり」、「つい昨日」といった意味を表す⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-form-tap-can-combine-with-other-adverbs⟧。北海道方言の他の時間表現として、副詞*ésir*は「さっき」や「直前」を意味する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-sir-means-a-little-while-ago⟧。副詞*teta*は「この間」を意味する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-adverb-teta-means-the-other-day⟧。時間名詞および副詞の*teeta*は「昔」や「過去」を意味する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-noun-adverb-teeta-means-long-ago⟧。さらに、時間副詞*tanto*は「今日」を意味し⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-tanto-means-today⟧、*núman*は「昨日」を意味し⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-n-man-means-yesterday⟧、*nisatta*は「明日」を意味する⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-temporal-adverb-nisatta-means-tomorrow⟧。

text.en: The Ainu verb lexicon has no morphological distinction between perfective and imperfective aspects ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-ainu-verb-lexicon-has-no-morphological-distinction⟧. To express that an event has already occurred before a certain reference point, auxiliaries such as *a* and *nisa* or auxiliary verb constructions such as *wa isam* and *wa okere* can be used ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--an-event-that-has-already-occurred-before-a⟧. The auxiliary *nisa* indicates that an event has already been realized, thereby indicating relative past when anchored to the speech time ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-auxiliary-nisa-indicates-that-an-event-has⟧. Forms such as *a*, *nisa*, and *wa okere* are fundamentally aspectual rather than temporal; they express past time only when used in clauses oriented to the present speech time, and in other contexts they do not necessarily refer to past events ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--forms-like-a-nisa-and-wa-okere-are⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の語彙そのものには完了相と未完了相の形態的な区別が存在しない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-ainu-verb-lexicon-has-no-morphological-distinction⟧。ある時点以前にすでに生じた事態を表す手段として、*a*や*nisa*などの助動詞や、*wa isam*、*wa okere*などの補助動詞形式が用いられる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--an-event-that-has-already-occurred-before-a⟧。助動詞*nisa*は事態がすでに実現したことを示し、発話時点に結びつけられた場合には相対的過去を表す⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--the-auxiliary-nisa-indicates-that-an-event-has⟧。*a*、*nisa*、*wa okere*などの形式は本来的にアスペクトに関わるものであって時制標識ではないため、現在の発話時点を基準にした文の中で用いられた場合にのみ過去を表し、文脈次第では過去の事象を指すとは限らない⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--forms-like-a-nisa-and-wa-okere-are⟧。

text.en: Future events that have not yet occurred can be expressed by auxiliary-like forms expressing volition or necessity, such as *kusu ne* or *kus ne* 'intend to', *oasi* 'will surely', *etokus* 'intend to / seem about to', and *etokoyki* 'be preparing to' ⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--future-events-that-have-not-yet-occurred-can⟧.
text.ja: 未だ事態が成立していない未来に起こることは、*kusu ne*および*kus ne*「〜するつもりだ」、*oasi*「きっと〜する」、*etokus*「〜するつもりだ、〜しそうだ」、*etokoyki*「〜する用意をしている」といった意志や必然性を表す助動詞的形式によって表すことができる⟦claim:tam/tenselessness-and-time-reference--future-events-that-have-not-yet-occurred-can⟧。
